title: AlgoExpert · Max Subset Sum No Adjacent

slides.heading: Max Subset Sum No Adjacent
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Max Subset Sum No Adjacent, a medium dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Max sum of positive ints with no two chosen elements adjacent.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Max sum of positive ints with no two chosen elements adjacent.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: At each index, either take it plus the best up to two back, or skip it.
slides.narration: At each index, either take it plus the best up to two back, or skip it.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: all subsets without neighbours → exponential
DP array best[i] → O(n) time, O(n) space
Only two previous values needed → O(1) space
slides.narration: Trying every non-adjacent subset is exponential. A DP where best i is the max of best i minus one and best i minus two plus the value is linear, and only the last two values are ever needed.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Keep the best up to i minus one and i minus two
2. Choose the max of skip or take
slides.narration: Step by step. First, keep the best up to i minus one and i minus two. Second, choose the max of skip or take. Third, slide forward.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: best[0] = 75 (take 75)
slides.narration: At 75: skipping keeps 0; taking adds 75 to the best two back. Taking wins, so the best is 75.

slides.narration: At 105: skipping keeps 75; taking adds 105 to the best two back. Taking wins, so the best is 105.

slides.narration: At 75: skipping keeps 195; taking adds 75 to the best two back. Skipping wins, so the best stays 195.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We keep prev and cur, both starting at zero. For each value, next is the max of cur and prev plus the value; then we slide: prev becomes cur and cur becomes next.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: An empty array gives zero. With negatives, choosing nothing is allowed, which the zero initial values handle.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: This is the classic house robber problem. The circular version runs the algorithm twice, excluding the first or last house.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: At each index, either take it plus the best up to two back, or skip it.
slides.narration: To recap Max Subset Sum No Adjacent: At each index, either take it plus the best up to two back, or skip it. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
